judgements.justification: A's checkable claims (Theorem 2 reduction to MGT, one-way theorems, matrix typo, Fig. 1d) are all correct; kvzq's mistaken rank-condition question in B did not lower its 7.
B's chair chose an oral on 8/7/6 with a top score of 'Top 50% of accepted' and no reviewer asking for an oral, on the chair's own reading.
B's kvzq praised briefly but at confidence 4 and with specific points (rank condition, assumptions, estimation); no high score rested on low-confidence enthusiasm.
No flaw was disclosed to one committee only; the authors conceded open completeness on both forums.
A did not discount h23K's depth critique, and B never heard it; no committee set aside a known flaw.
iUkv in B rose from 5 to 6 after the notation answers; no score in A moved.
Only A's h23K raised that Theorem 2's surrogate set reduces the problem to the MGT loop, a checkable depth concern B never weighed.

Both saw missing experiments and dense notation; A's yA7o held experiments against the paper and A's chair called it 'very difficult to follow', while B's kvzq excused experiments and B treated notation as fixable.
Neither chair adopted a single reviewer's position; A followed four uniform 6s.
No reviewer moved because of other reviews.
The authors answered h23K's Theorem 2 point only with general claims, but h23K never re-engaged and nothing shows the gap held its score down.
A's yA7o spent 2 hours, checked no proofs, asked for experiments on a theory paper, and its update named no specific gap, yet its 6 counted unchallenged.
No chair went below its reviewers' majority.
A's chair stated no positive view of its own beyond 'reviewers saw merit'; it followed the scores, not a threshold over its own reading.
No below-threshold score held on a peripheral point; iUkv rose to 6.
Both committees evaluated an identification-theory contribution.
B's iUkv could not follow the results or verify the proofs, yet rose from 5 to 6 on notation clarifications and promised revisions.
A's yA7o required experiments of an identification-theory paper, while B's kvzq said a theory paper should not be penalised for lacking them.
No praise in B rested on a wrong factual claim.
No reviewer kept a below-threshold score after its concern was answered; iUkv raised its score.

A's yA7o refused experiments and the continuous case put off as future work and A's chair still judged the paper hard to follow, while B credited promised notation fixes as making the problems fixable.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from an unedited score.
No off-record extra reviewer.
B's reviewers also found the notation dense (iUkv) and assumptions opaque (kvzq); no expert read the text as clear.
iUkv stated why it raised its score.
No chair set aside a silent detractor.
B's 8 (9UEy) and 7 (kvzq) rested on no stated proof check and neither argued in the discussion, so no invested champion is on record.
No partial-reading reviewer claimed high confidence.
All reviewers accepted the identification framing.
B's meta-review justifies the oral with one generic sentence, 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution', and no case for an award tier.
Neither committee checked baselines against published results; it is a theory paper and familiarity differences show only as confidence.
Neither meta-review misstates the reviewers' final positions.
A's 6Pv4 judged the paper better suited to a journal, one of A's grounds for a poster, while B raised no venue concern.
A had no misreading low-scoring detractor; all rated 6.
No new results were posted to one committee only.
A had no high-confidence expert review; its top confidence was 3.
yA7o's 2021-09-10 update did not change its score.
B's verbal assessments ('a very strong contribution', 'relevant and significant') are more favourable than A's, so the gap is not scale leniency.
A did not judge a headline claim overstated; B's chair asked only for an abstract clarification and still gave an oral.

added.name: Unsure reviewers converged on marginal-accept scores
added.definition: Reviewers in one committee who could not check the technical core each settled on the marginal-accept rating at low or middling confidence, so the flat scores carried no signal for an award and the area chair read them as a poster-level verdict, while the other committee's reviewers committed to higher ratings.
added.justification: R27 needs an invested champion and R36 an outweighed expert; neither names the mechanism here, where a whole panel unable to check the core hedged at the same borderline score and the chair took that uniformity as the verdict.

reasoning: Committee B gave an oral on 8/7/6 while A gave a poster on four 6s, with no factual error found in either. The oral is B's chair's own call, argued in one generic sentence (R02, R30), helped by a rebuttal that lifted a reviewer who could not check the core (R06, R17). A saw a depth critique B never heard (R07), weighed missing experiments and dense notation more heavily (R08, R18, R21), raised journal fit (R33), and counted a thin review (R12). The stage 1 candidate that A's low-confidence reviewers all hedged at 6 is not covered by any existing reason, so R40 was added.
